Continuation Model • By LC Trades

The 9 Matrix

A continuation model built around an efficient trend, a pullback into the 9 or 21 EMA, and a clean rejection toward the active draw.

Read delivery Wait for location Confirm rejection Execute with rules

Chapter 01 Foundation

EMA Framework

01
EMA

An exponential moving average gives more weight to recent candles, so it reacts faster to current price than a simple moving average.

9 EMA

The faster average. It marks the location for a shallower continuation pullback.

21 EMA

The slower average. It can hold a deeper retracement before continuation.

Read the EMA state
9/21 EMA Crossover

When the 9 crosses above the 21, the bullish cross supports continuation higher. When the 9 crosses below the 21, the bearish cross supports continuation lower. The signal is strongest when price is also delivering efficiently toward the active draw.

EMA Consolidation = No Trade

If price closes above, then below, then above again—or price is moving back and forth between the 9 and 21—the market is consolidating on the EMAs. Wait for clean direction and rejection instead of forcing a continuation trade.

NO CLEAR SIDE = NO TRADEFlat averages, alternating closes, and repeated movement through both EMAs identify consolidation. The EMAs are useful here because they tell you when to stay out.

Chapter 02 Context

Psychology of the Pullback

A pause in delivery is often a reset of participation, not proof that the larger move has changed its mind.

02
The tired dog

A tired dog that has been running needs a break; it does not suddenly want to run the other way. An efficient market can retrace and rebalance without reversing its destination.

Reset, not reversal

As price pulls back, late traders who entered from FOMO may lose conviction while earlier participants decide whether their position can survive the reset.

Weak holders exit

The retracement can stop out weak holders and invite premature countertrend traders who mistake a pause for a complete change in direction.

Liquidity forms

Those exits and opposing entries create liquidity. If the original delivery remains intact, that liquidity can help fuel the next move toward the active draw.

THE MARKET NEEDS A BREAKA pullback can reset an efficient move without changing its destination.

Chapter 03 Direction

Trend and Objective

The 9 Matrix reads the quality of delivery first, then uses the EMA as the location where that delivery may react.

03
Efficient Trend

A consistent trend shows spread and efficiency after a pullback: directional candles, visible expansion, and limited overlap.

Draw on Liquidity

Locate the liquidity that price is likely delivering toward. A continuation has purpose when the expected path still points to an active draw.

Re-soup Objective

When the market has displaced and rebalanced, use the remaining objective to judge whether the continuation still has room to deliver.

LOCATION, NOT DEFINITIONThe EMA supplies a reaction location; it does not define trend. Price delivery and the active objective do.
9:30–10:10 NEW YORKThe 9 Matrix is evaluated only inside this window.

Chapter 04 Confirmation

Valid EMA Rejection

The reaction has to agree with the established trend. A touch of an EMA alone is only a location, never a completed setup.

04
Bullish rejection

Price may touch or wick through the 9 or 21 EMA, but the rejection candle cannot close bearish. The close must preserve the bullish continuation idea.

Bearish rejection

Price may touch or wick through the 9 or 21 EMA, but the rejection candle cannot close bullish. The close must preserve the bearish continuation idea.

A valid rejection may touch or wick through either the 9 or 21 EMA, but its close cannot oppose the established trend.

NO REJECTION = NO TRADEPrice may wick through the EMA, but the rejection candle cannot close opposite the established trend.

Chapter 05 Confluence

Internal SMT With ES

NQ and ES often travel together. When their internal swings disagree during a pullback, that disagreement can add context to a continuation setup.

05
Bullish Continuation

One correlated market takes an internal low while the other holds its corresponding low. That mismatch can show the pullback collecting liquidity instead of building a true reversal.

Bearish Continuation

One correlated market takes an internal high while the other holds its corresponding high. The mismatch can support a continuation lower when the rest of the model still agrees.

OPTIONAL CONFLUENCEInternal SMT is optional confluence. It strengthens the model but never replaces trend, draw, time window, or a valid EMA rejection.

Chapter 06 Execution

Entry Styles

Both entries require the same context. The choice is between getting in earlier and waiting for more proof from the rejection candle.

06
Standard Entry

Enter at the close of the valid rejection candle.

Aggressive Entry

Enter on the immediate rejection from the 9 or 21 EMA before the candle closes. The price may be better, but confirmation risk is higher.

EARLY VS. CONFIRMEDThe aggressive entry is earlier and less confirmed. The standard entry waits for candle-close confirmation before committing.

Chapter 07 Trade Tape

Two Trades. Four Decisions.

The chart does not change because the entry style changes. Read the context first, then choose whether to enter early, wait for the close, or manage a confirmed runner.

07
01
Bias + confluence

Bearish SMT confirms the rejection

The day is already bearish. NQ takes the corresponding high, but ES does not confirm that strength, creating bearish SMT.

NQ rejects from the 21 EMA, works back through the 21 and 9, and closes below the averages. ES also rejects the 21 and prints multiple closes below the 9 before entry.

Read it in order: bearish bias → high taken on NQ → bearish SMT with ES → 21/9 rejection → continuation lower.
02
Earlier · higher risk

Aggressive entry at the 9 tap

This is the earlier version of the same bullish trade. SMT supports the bullish idea, the draw remains higher, and price is delivering with speed and efficiency.

The entry is taken as price taps and rejects the 9 EMA instead of waiting for the candle to finish.

Trade-off: the tap can provide a better price, but the candle has not closed, so confirmation risk is higher.
03
Later · more proof

Safer entry after the close

This is the same bullish setup entered at a different point. Instead of buying the 9 tap, wait for the rejection candle to close and confirm continuation.

The target is the planned 1:1 based on the actual stop distance. It is not an automatic 30-point target.

Trade-off: the candle close gives more confirmation, but the entry comes later and may offer less favorable pricing.
04
Runner management

Holding toward all-time highs

An early entry can sometimes become a runner when the active draw is much higher, especially on a day delivering toward all-time highs.

After valid displacement, the 9 EMA can be used as a visual trailing guide. In this example, holding the move could capture roughly 180 points—nearly 200—rather than exiting at the first target.

Management distinction: the normal plan can still take the 1:1. The extended hold is optional and requires a separate trailing rule.
SAME MODEL, DIFFERENT EXECUTIONAggressive, confirmed, and runner management are separate decisions. Define the entry and exit style before the trade instead of changing rules after price moves.

Chapter 08 Protection

Initial Stop Protection

Before the trade proves itself, structure defines where the original setup is invalid. EMA trailing begins later, after the position is profitable and continuation is confirmed.

08
Initial Stop

Place the initial stop beyond a valid PD array or the displacement candle protecting the setup. For bullish continuation, the stop sits below that protection.

Bearish Protection

For bearish continuation, the initial stop sits above the valid PD array or displacement candle that would invalidate the original setup.

Structure Protects the Initial StopEMAs Guide the Profit Trail once displacement confirms the trade and the position has moved into profit.
Management sequence
Enter
Confirm Displacement
Begin Trailing

Trailing is encouraged only after valid displacement confirms continuation. Protect the trade after confirmation, but leave enough room for price to continue toward the active draw; this model does not prescribe one mechanical trailing interval.

Chapter 09 Trade Management

Trail With the EMAs

Once the trade is in profit and directional displacement confirms continuation, the EMAs can become a moving defense that protects profit while leaving room for a larger move.

09
9 EMA — First Line of Defense

Use the 9 EMA when you want to manage the trade more aggressively. Trail the stop slightly beyond the 9 so profit is protected sooner while price continues to respect the faster average.

21 EMA — Second Line of Defense

Use the 21 EMA when you want to give a longer-term trade more room. Trail slightly beyond the 21 so normal pullbacks have space without immediately ending the runner.

Choose Before the Pullback

Decide whether the trade will use the tighter 9 or the looser 21 based on the management plan. Do not switch EMAs impulsively just because a candle creates pressure.

Profit-management sequence
Trade Reaches Profit
Confirm Displacement
Select 9 or 21
Trail Beyond the EMA
AGGRESSIVE OR PATIENTThe 9 protects sooner and may exit earlier. The 21 gives the trade more room and accepts a larger pullback in exchange for the chance to stay with a bigger move.

Chapter 10 Profit Protection

Don't Let a Winning Trade Turn Against You

Once price has moved into profit and confirmed the trade, management changes from proving the idea to protecting what the market has already given you.

10
Protect the Profit

After directional displacement, bring the trade under an EMA-based trailing plan. Do not let a confirmed winner travel all the way back to the original full-risk stop.

Respect the Selected Defense

Use the 9 for tighter protection or the 21 for more breathing room. Trail slightly beyond the selected average and respond when price stops respecting it.

Read Changing Delivery

Overlapping candles, lost efficiency, repeated EMA closes, or divergence with ES can show that continuation is weakening. Protect first instead of assuming the move must resume.

Opposing SMT WarningIf NQ and ES stop following suit and an SMT forms against the open trade, trail aggressively. That divergence can warn that price may wick through the EMA or displace against the position. Protect the profit rather than giving the trade unnecessary room.
SEPARATE THE TARGET FROM THE RUNNERThe planned 1:1 can still be taken. Holding for a larger move is a separate management choice and should already have a defined EMA trail.

Chapter 11 Full Model

The 9 Matrix

Read the sequence in order. The matrix organizes the context, confirmation, entry, and management rules into one repeatable review process.

11
Required Optional Confluence Trader's Choice
Phase One

Context

01
  1. 01 · Efficient TrendRequired

    Directional spread, expansion, and limited overlap—not consolidation between the EMAs.

  2. 02 · Active DrawRequired

    A draw or re-soup objective remains in the direction of continuation.

  3. 03 · Time WindowRequired

    Evaluate the setup between 9:30 and 10:10 a.m. New York.

Phase Two

Trigger

02
  1. 04 · EMA LocationRequired

    Price pulls back to the 9 or 21 and gives a usable continuation location.

  2. 05 · Valid RejectionRequired

    The rejection candle closes with the established direction, not against it.

  3. 06 · Internal SMT With ESOptional Confluence

    SMT can strengthen the setup, but it does not replace trend, draw, timing, or rejection.

Phase Three

Management

03
  1. 07 · Entry StyleTrader's Choice

    Enter aggressively on the EMA reaction or wait for the confirmed candle close.

  2. 08 · Initial StopRequired

    Protect the original setup beyond valid structure or the displacement candle.

  3. 09 · Displace and TrailTrader's Choice

    After profit and displacement, use the tighter 9 or looser 21 EMA trail. Tighten aggressively on opposing SMT.

SMT IS OPTIONALInternal SMT with ES is optional confluence inside the matrix. The required structure of the setup must already be present before SMT adds weight.
CONSOLIDATION FILTERIf price alternates above and below the EMAs or moves repeatedly between them, the Context phase fails and there is no trade.
